fail_reasons.loss_coefficient: K against Borda-Carnot misses the 5% band on the finest mesh. This is not a convergence failure of the solver: the reattachment length of the same runs is mesh converged to a few tenths of a percent and the two recirculation bubbles are symmetric to round-off, while all three bookkeepings of K (raw inlet-to-outlet total-pressure drop, resolved-wall-shear corrected, and linear-decay extrapolated to the step plane) stay separated from 0.5625 by more than the band. Borda-Carnot assumes complete mixing: a uniform downstream profile, so that the whole excess kinetic energy of the inlet jet is dissipated. At Re_D = 100 the jet reattaches and redevelops without mixing, part of the inlet kinetic energy survives in the parabolic profile (alpha = 1.543), and the measured static pressure recovery is larger than the momentum balance with uniform profiles allows. The coefficient is therefore reported with its definition attached and flagged FAIL rather than averaged towards the theory.
fail_reasons.order_loss_coefficient: The observed order of the loss coefficient could not be established: the three levels do not form a monotone sequence, which is the signature of a definition whose dominant error is not the mesh spacing (the extrapolation window and the inlet representation dominate). The reattachment length of the same runs is monotone and well resolved, so the failure is attributed to the K diagnostic, not to the flow field.
fail_reasons.reattachment: The reattachment length passes its mesh-convergence band against the Richardson limit. An experiment-fitted L_r/D for this exact configuration (planar, symmetric, AR = 4, Re_D = 100, uniform inlet) was not available offline, so the reference is the order-verified Richardson limit of this solver's own mesh sequence (10% band) together with the exact symmetry of the two bubbles. This is declared explicitly instead of quoting a literature number that could not be checked.
fail_reasons.third_level: The D/64 level, which would have kept the inlet opening exactly face aligned at a finer spacing, was not affordable in this session: the solver is explicit, the step count is set by the physical time to steady state and the cell count grows quadratically, while the shared host ran at load average 370-600 and the loong64 compute cluster cannot execute this library (its torch build requires GLIBCXX_3.4.32, absent from the nodes). The published ladder is the aligned sequence that ran to stationarity.
